doc.title: J. Leo Rayhill interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 23, 2007

title: WHC radio and boogie-woogie records
summary: He first DJed on Hamilton's WHC, playing boogie-woogie records bought for 35 cents; tuition was $450.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Oh right. So you got your first taste of being a jazz DJ here at Hamilton? Was it WHC?

WHC. The wonderful thing, I remember I loved boogie woogie at the time, I used to play a lot of boogie when — I loved those Albert Ammons and Pete Johnson. Those guys were just great. And then you could buy the record for 35 cents.
And what was your tuition here? Do you recall? What did it cost to go to Hamilton?
